Business goal: Allow backend features and controlled root-admin operators to send real transactional emails through a provider-agnostic platform seam.
User outcome: The platform can send a real test email and later feature-owned workflows can trigger outbound email without each feature implementing provider logic.
Notes / constraints: Email is the first implemented channel under notificationDelivery. V1 uses a provider-agnostic seam with one real provider adapter, currently assumed to be Resend. The seam must support real delivery now while remaining swappable later. Automatic background retry is out of scope for v1 but the model must not block it later. Content may be simple text in v1. A logical outbound email record and at least one attempt record must be created for every send.
Tenant context rule: not applicable inside the shared delivery seam; tenant context may be attached by the caller feature as metadata but is not resolved by the platform seam itself
Explicitly denied roles: all tenant actors and unauthenticated callers
Authorization summary: Internal feature calls can send through the shared seam. Any operator-triggered send path is root-admin controlled only. No tenant-member or public caller can send email directly in v1.

Granted role / boundary: shared platform boundary plus root-admin operator proof path
Frontend visibility rule: No general frontend UI is required in v1 beyond any future root-admin shell wiring.

Response contract: Returns logical email record metadata, latest attempt metadata, provider name, status, and timestamps suitable for operator confirmation.
